purpose: Expand the exact v8.5.2 Fourier-current contraction into a finite rank-generating state sum over GF(3), isolating the remaining exponential object without losing the Hamiltonian exposed-port order.

starting_identity.closed_network: m canonical six-port quotient wires and 3m physical NEQ splice edges forming a perfect matching of all exposed ports
starting_identity.current_identity: Z = 3^(-2m) * sum_{k in K} prod_e h(k_e) * prod_v A_v(k)
starting_identity.base_constraints: K is the GF(3) linear subspace defined by one signed current-conservation equation at every wire

rank_state_expansion.edge_state: For each splice edge e choose free or zero. The free term contributes coefficient -1; the zero term contributes coefficient 3 and appends the coordinate row k_e=0.
rank_state_expansion.wire_state: For each wire v choose one symbol in {0,+,-}. Symbol 0 contributes coefficient -2 and no extra row. Symbol + contributes coefficient 3 and appends l_{v,+}=0. Symbol - contributes coefficient 3 and appends l_{v,-}=0.
rank_state_expansion.matrix: R(S,tau) consists of all m conservation rows, the coordinate rows for selected zero-edges S, and one local VP/VM row for every nonzero tau_v.
rank_state_expansion.term_count: For a state (S,tau), the number of compatible currents is exactly 3^(3m-rank_GF3(R(S,tau))).
rank_state_expansion.exact_formula: Z = 3^(-2m) * sum_{S subseteq E} sum_{tau in {0,+,-}^V} (-1)^(3m-|S|) * 3^|S| * [prod_v w(tau_v)] * 3^(3m-rank(R(S,tau))), where w(0)=-2 and w(+)=w(-)=3.

structural_interpretation.object: partition-constrained ternary linear rank-generating state sum
structural_interpretation.ground_rows: optional edge-coordinate rows together with two optional local linear-form rows {l_{v,+},l_{v,-}} per wire, over the fixed conservation row space
structural_interpretation.partition_rule: At each wire at most one of the two local rows may be selected, with a third null state carrying coefficient -2.
structural_interpretation.why_not_v6_8_loop: v6.8 ruled out solvers that factor only through the isomorphism class of the full transition matroid. The present matrix is built from the actual Hamiltonian exposed-port incidence and the ordered VP/VM forms, so it retains data explicitly allowed by the v6.8 not-killed list rather than replacing the graph by its transition-matroid isomorphism class.
structural_interpretation.known_context: Multimatroid/interlace/transition polynomials naturally encode rank or circuit-partition state sums, but identifying this exact weighted ternary specialization does not by itself provide a polynomial-time evaluator.

exact_two_wire_control.method: For every permutation matching the six exposed ports of wire 1 to the six exposed ports of wire 2, compare direct enumeration of 12^2 quotient assignments against the rank-state expansion using exact GF(3) Gaussian elimination.

gained: Every exponential current assignment has been eliminated in favor of a rank-generating state sum whose individual terms are polynomial-time Gaussian-rank evaluations.
The exact remaining source of exponential growth is isolated as the 24^m choice of edge zero/free states and local {0,+,-} transition states.
The representation remains sensitive to Hamiltonian port order and therefore does not fall under the v6.8 full-transition-matroid invariance barrier.
not_gained: No polynomial-time evaluation of the full 24^m rank-state sum.
No polynomial-size witness-reconstruction algorithm from a compressed rank evaluation.

next_target.name: E8_C4_GF3_CHARACTERISTIC_POLYNOMIAL_COLLAPSE_V8_5_4
next_target.directive: Sum the entire optional edge-coordinate layer analytically for each fixed local transition assignment tau. Test whether the 2^(3m) edge states collapse to one exact characteristic-polynomial/full-support-code evaluation for the GF(3) column matroid generated by conservation plus selected VP/VM rows. Preserve Hamiltonian port order and explicitly keep the remaining outer 3^m local-state sum visible.
next_target.mandatory_firewall: Do not call the resulting expression polynomial time unless both the characteristic-polynomial evaluations and the outer local-state sum are compressed with polynomial state count, polynomial bitlength, exact decision equivalence and witness reconstruction.

sources: Robert Brijder and Hendrik Jan Hoogeboom, Interlace Polynomials for Multimatroids and Delta-Matroids, 2010/2012.
Robert Brijder, Orienting Transversals and Transition Polynomials of Multimatroids, Advances in Applied Mathematics 94 (2018), 120-155.
Lorenzo Traldi, The transition matroid of a 4-regular graph: an introduction, European Journal of Combinatorics 50 (2015), 180-207.
